summary: Jodrie Hill in Milan: a wooden tower built 1925 was later replaced by the Milan Hill tower; 2014 and 2020 hikers disagree on what remains.

facts.status_note: Listed as removed; the Forest Fire Lookout Association list shows no standing tower.

events.note: Wooden tower, per a 2014 hiking report; meant to replace a tower on Cambridge Black.
Milan Hill tower built in 1932 (NHLR). The 2014 report says it replaced the Jodrie Hill tower. No readable source dates the removal of the Jodrie Hill tower.

evidence.supports: Built 1925 to replace the Cambridge Black tower; later replaced by the Milan Hill tower
evidence.quote: This peak once had a wooden firetower, but no longer. Built in 1925 it was meant to replace the tower that once stood on Cambridge Black, but was itself replaced by the one that still stands on Milan Hill a short distance away.
Next up was Jodrie Hill (elevation 1640') located in Milan, New Hampshire.

evidence.supports: 2014 summit: four foundation holes, no other remains
evidence.quote: On the summit we found four holes drilled for foundation poles. But no other remains were present.

evidence.supports: Milan Hill tower, 45 ft steel, built 1932
evidence.quote: the 45' steel tower with standard NH wooden cab was built on Milan Hill in 1932
Mountains which Once Had a Fire Tower

evidence.supports: 2020 hiker found no artifacts of any former tower
evidence.quote: Completely surrounded by woods, there was nothing to see and no artifacts of any former tower.
this hill is surrounded by private residences

notes_for_editor: The 1925 build date and the replacement by the Milan Hill tower rest on one 2014 blog. NHLR dates only the Milan Hill tower (1932). A 2019 firelookouts Instagram post reportedly gives 1925 built and 1932 removed, but the page would not load, so it is not cited. The 2014 and 2020 hikers disagree on remains (four foundation holes versus no artifacts); the 2020 writer may have searched a different spot, so the story reports both. No readable source confirms public access. The 2020 report describes approaching across fields by private homes; do not publish directions or route details.
